channel.title: Xiaoyuan — Systems Writing
channel.description: Writing about distributed data systems, ML platforms, and AI agents.

item.title: Identity Must Flow Through the Agent Call Chain
item.description: A file update that crosses a queue shows how an agent can still prove who is acting for whom when execution resumes asynchronously.

item.title: Why a while Loop Is Not Yet an Agent Runtime
item.description: One Tool write with an unknown outcome shows why a simple Agent Loop can lose track of the task's actual state.

item.title: Middleware Hooks Need Ordering and Failure Contracts
item.description: A conflict among policy, request transformation, and tracing shows why Agent Runtime Hooks need explicit mutation, short-circuit, error, and replay semantics.

item.title: Run, Turn, Step, and Task Are Different State Machines
item.description: A report still being converted shows why one status cannot represent a user goal, model round trip, logical action, and background work.

item.title: A Tool Lifecycle Is More Than a Function Call
item.description: A file write shows why a Tool needs a complete lifecycle across model selection, trusted execution, and result delivery.

item.title: Context Assembly Is a Policy Engine
item.description: Conflicting history, memory, and files show why Context Assembly cannot be just message concatenation.

item.title: Structured Concurrency in Python Agent Runtimes
item.description: A group of ownerless Tool Tasks shows how TaskGroup makes concurrent work awaitable, cancellable, and able to propagate failures.

item.title: Agent Tool Surfaces: Eager, Deferred, and On-Demand Discovery
item.description: Select eager, deferred, and disabled capabilities from a Tool registry by task and permission, then evaluate the trade-offs in tokens, latency, and discovery recall.

item.title: Define the Grain Before Modeling Agent Activity
item.description: A Tool retry shows why an Agent Run, a logical action, and an execution Attempt cannot share one row of data.

item.title: State Machines, Leases, and Idempotency for Long-Running Tasks
item.description: Reliable long-running tasks depend on explicit state machines, expiring ownership, fencing tokens, and idempotent side effects—not on avoiding retries.

item.title: Tool Schemas Are Model-Facing APIs
item.description: A tool schema is not a copy of a backend DTO. It is an interface that helps a model select a capability, generate arguments, and recover from errors.

item.title: Notes on Spark Adaptive Query Execution
item.description: Adaptive Query Execution lets Spark SQL revise its physical plan using runtime statistics, including coalescing shuffle partitions, handling skewed joins, and changing join strategies.

item.title: How to Use Spark Transformations Correctly
item.description: A Spark transformation describes lazy, distributed, recomputable work. Using transformations correctly requires understanding actions, closures, side effects, shuffles, partitions, and persistence.

item.title: Spark Data Skew — How to Identify, Diagnose, and Fix It
item.description: Data skew is not simply a slow job. It is an imbalance in how data is distributed across partitions. This article uses the Spark UI, key distributions, and execution plans to diagnose and address skew in joins and aggregations.

item.title: Notes on Spark Resource Requests and Data Representation on YARN
item.description: A practical example of Spark resource-request settings on YARN, followed by considerations for data representation in Spark.

item.title: Apache Spark Resource Management on YARN
item.description: An overview of Apache Spark resource management and the application model used when Spark runs on YARN.

item.title: Understanding Linux Process Memory Usage
item.description: A concise guide to VSS, RSS, PSS, and USS when inspecting the memory usage of a Linux process.

item.title: CMD or ENTRYPOINT in a Dockerfile?
item.description: CMD and ENTRYPOINT serve similar purposes in a Dockerfile, but their behavior—especially when combined—requires careful attention.

item.title: Why Use Tini as a Docker Container Entrypoint?
item.description: What is Tini, and why is it useful as the entrypoint of a container?

item.title: A New Beginning
item.description: Starting again with notes on technology and personal reflections.
